question: Show me how to take Punctual Pros nationwide
html:
Taking Punctual Pros Nationwide

Punctual Pros can follow the Smith + Howard growth plan in four phases. The sequence is: fill the Central-PA core, repeat the Horvath deal across the Mid-Atlantic, build an I-81/I-95 hub, then consolidate inside the Authority Brands system. AI-led booking and memberships should drive margin at each step (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

The precedent

  • Over about 3.7 years, Smith + Howard grew from ~100 professionals in one Atlanta office to ~800 across 11 locations. It made nine acquisitions, grew revenue ~4x and sold to TPG Growth in August 2026 (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • Punctual Pros starts from a comparable base:
  • ~$22M est. FY2025 revenue
  • 25 territories
  • 248 core zips with ~1.0M housing units
  • one out-of-state add-on, Horvath on the Jersey Shore

Four expansion phases

  • Phase 1 (months 0-12): Densify the core and the 195 best nearby ZIP codes (144 PA, 51 MD). Close 1-2 tuck-ins from the 61-company screen.
  • Phase 2 (months 9-24): Pursue the 54 mapped Authority territories in PA, NJ, MD, DE and southern NY that Punctual Pros does not own. Expect competition from 17 PE sponsors.
  • Phase 3 (months 18-36): Build a Mid-Atlantic hub covering Baltimore-DC, Richmond, the Philadelphia suburbs and Pittsburgh.
  • Phase 4: Become the national consolidator in the One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky system. That system has 1,066 outlets and $831M of reported revenue; Punctual Pros holds ~2.3% today.

Every row is a modelling assumption, not a reported figure (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

What sponsor exits teach

Across 17 companies, sponsors who sold for more followed a similar order (Home-services company case studies):

  • They hired an integrator or professional CEO early.
  • They added about one company per quarter, then accelerated.
  • They ran every brand on one system.
  • They built memberships. Champions reached ~83 members per technician and sold at a reported ~18.5x.
  • They owned the technician pipeline through training centers and academies.

The failures carry the clearest warning. Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint added brands faster than they integrated them.

First tuck-in targets

The top-ranked names in the add-on screen are (Punctual Pros add-on targets):

  • Lancaster Plumbing (fit score 84)
  • the Ron Williams West Chester tri-brand group (82)
  • C&C on the Jersey Shore (82)
  • Zimmerman (80)
  • PHE South Jersey (80)

Revenue and headcount for these targets are missing because company-data enrichment was unavailable. Diligence requests should fill that gap.

Open data gaps

  • Financing: The context has no debt capacity, leverage or equity-check figures. Lender term sheets and a BSP fund allocation model would answer this.
  • AI booking impact: ServiceTitan reports 70% booking. A pilot measuring Punctual Pros' own booked-call rate is needed before relying on that figure.

Next actions

  1. Recruit an integrator COO before the second tuck-in closes.
  2. Request financials from Lancaster Plumbing and the Ron Williams group, and model leverage for both deals.
  3. Pilot the 24/7 AI voice dispatcher and missed-call text-back in the core zips. Measure booked-call lift against the month-0 baseline.
  4. Set a membership target per technician and track it monthly against the roadmap.
